html:
A city on the Niger River in the far west of Niger, made capital of the French colony in 1926 in place of Zinder.

When the French chose it, Niamey was a cluster of Zarma, Fula and Hausa villages. It grew slowly until independence, then fast, swelled by people fleeing the Sahel droughts of the 1970s and 1980s. It is now home to more than a million people and has the national museum, where the remains of the Tree of Tenere are kept. Being close to Mali and Burkina Faso, it has been exposed to the jihadist wars of the region.
sum: A city on the Niger River in the far west of Niger, made capital of the French colony in 1926 in place of Zinder.
